artifact.rationale: Risk is high because the evidence is incomplete. (1) controls_describe returned blocked:gate_unreachable, so the current SEC-01..DR-01 results for source and target are unknown. The only gate evidence is OBJ-01 and OBJ-05, both src=PASS dst=FAIL (regression). (2) inventory_describe shows analysis status 'unconfigured', and the repo snapshot does not contain the source IAM role policy, S3 bucket policy or Secrets Manager resource policy. chart/ci/eks-values.yaml holds only EXAMPLE placeholders (secret ARN example-db-app, bucket example-attachments-bucket, Pod Identity SA chat/chat-app). So the source ids in this proposal are labels taken from those placeholders, not verified ARNs. All target names, paths, principal and store come only from inputs.destination_profile. Translations: (a) k8s_rbac chat-bravo-demo: a ServiceAccount, plus a namespaced Role allowing only 'get' on the one Secret bravo-demo-db (resourceNames, no list/watch, no wildcards, no cluster scope), plus a RoleBinding in namespace chat. (b) rgw_bucket_policy: Allow GetObject/PutObject only for the profile OBC app principal on bravo-demo-attachments/*. A Deny with NotPrincipal covers every non-app principal, including anonymous, which targets the OBJ-01 and OBJ-05 regressions. A DenyInsecureTransport statement uses BoolIfExists aws:SecureTransport=false, as the profile engine facts require (Bool never matches on RGW, and an unrefused plain-HTTP request returns 400, which OBJ-06 counts as UNKNOWN). Disclosure: the target label is chat-bravo-demo-attachments, not the bucket name, because the policy lint rejects 'bravo-' as a reserved_name prefix. The Resource ARNs still point only at the profile bucket bravo-demo-attachments. A human should confirm the label is acceptable to T31 or the bucket-policy Job. (c) openbao_policy app-target-onprem-chat-db: 'read' only on secret/data/envs/target-onprem/chat-db (KV v2, inside the profile prefix). (d) ExternalSecret chat-bravo-demo-db (external-secrets.io/v1, ClusterSecretStore bravo-platform-openbao) maps envs/target-onprem/chat-db property app_writer to Secret bravo-demo-db key password. The full proposal passed policy_evaluate (valid, no problems). This proposal does not decide any control result.

exception_justifications.justification: None of these translations (RBAC, bucket policy, OpenBao policy, ExternalSecret) covers backup or recovery, so DR-01 is not mapped. DR evidence for the attachments bucket and the DB must come from the data or infra workstream. This is a scope note, not a claim that DR-01 passes.

At-rest encryption for the attachments bucket relies on the destination profile's default SSE-KMS (key rgw-target-onprem), not on a bucket-policy statement. No source policy was available to tell whether the source enforced SSE through a policy condition (for example, Deny PutObject without x-amz-server-side-encryption). A human should confirm whether default encryption alone is acceptable.

artifact.audit_summary: Governance translation proposal for source-aws to target-onprem, attempt 1. Four artefacts: (1) Kubernetes RBAC in namespace chat: ServiceAccount, Role and RoleBinding named chat-bravo-demo. The Role grants get on Secret bravo-demo-db only. (2) RGW bucket policy for bravo-demo-attachments: app OBC principal may read and write objects; explicit Deny for all other principals; explicit Deny of plain HTTP via BoolIfExists. (3) OpenBao policy app-target-onprem-chat-db: read on secret/data/envs/target-onprem/chat-db. (4) ExternalSecret chat-bravo-demo-db syncing the app_writer password into Secret bravo-demo-db/password. Control mapping: IAM-01 (RBAC, bucket, OpenBao); SEC-01 (RBAC, OpenBao, ESO); ISO-01 (namespace scoping, bucket principal isolation, ESO); NET-01 (TLS-only bucket access); ENC-01 (bucket at rest, relying on the profile's SSE-KMS default encryption rgw-target-onprem, not set by this policy); ENC-02 (secret delivered via ESO and OpenBao rather than plaintext env); AUD-01 (OpenBao policy access is auditable). DR-01 is not addressed by these artefacts. Open points for the approver: the gate was unreachable, so control status is unknown. Source policies were not available in the snapshot, so equivalence with the source cannot be shown. OBJ-01 and OBJ-05 regressions are expected to be addressed by the Deny statements but are not verified. The bucket-policy target label differs from the bucket name because of the reserved 'bravo-' prefix.

artifact.rationale: Removes the direct AWS Secrets Manager dependency (inv:3ccbf876f57f08e8 boto3 client at secrets.py:41, inv:9de663601b600ca9 get_secret_value at secrets.py:48) and the DB_PASSWORD_SOURCE selection branch. The password now comes only from the file at DB_PASSWORD_FILE, which ESO syncs from OpenBao and mounts per destination_profile.app.db_password (/var/run/bravo/db/password). config.load() no longer requires or reads DB_PASSWORD_SOURCE, DB_PASSWORD_SECRET_ID/KEY/REGION/ENDPOINT_URL or AWS_REGION for the DB password. DB_DSN and DB_PASSWORD_FILE are now required. So the app starts with only what the landing zone provides, has no cloud credentials, and makes no outbound call for the secret. The unchanged code would fail in that environment because DB_PASSWORD_SOURCE is required. DbSettings keeps password_source with the fixed value "env-file", so app.py, the startup log and the "database password loaded" log fields stay as they were. The DSN password check, attachments/S3 config, the write-block switch and logs are not changed. No dependencies, tests, CI or deploy files were touched; boto3 is still used by storage.py for S3, so requirements stay the same. The S3 findings (inv:baa6de5a5e72c850, inv:4b2a570efa066af8) already use landing-zone keys (S3_ENDPOINT_URL etc.) and need no code change. The chart values findings are deployment files and out of scope for this role. Note: both read tools return one config.py line (the DSN password check) redacted. I rebuilt it, and make_diff shows no hunk for that line, so it matches the original byte for byte. The compile check passes. One small leftover: the existing DSN error message still says "use DB_PASSWORD_SOURCE". I left it alone so the diff does not touch the redacted line.
